response.draft:
Slide 1: Open When Our Neighbors Can Come
Fernwood Tool Library, Alder Falls
A proposal to the Alder Falls Community Fund
$46,500 a year for two years ($93,000 in all) to open evenings and Saturdays
Sample organization. Fernwood Tool Library and every person named here are fictional.

Slide 2: What Members Told Us
In May 2026, 512 members answered our survey
47% said our hours are what keeps them from borrowing more
The next answers were far behind: "the tool I wanted was out" (19%) and parking (11%)
Many work weekday afternoons and can't reach us before we close at 6 p.m.
"I've walked past at 6:15 more times than I can count. The lights are on and the door is locked."

Slide 3: Millbrook Is Missing Out
Millbrook has 22% of the city's renters
Only 9% of our members live there
61% of Millbrook members who answered named our hours, more than any other group
Most of them work shifts

Slide 4: The Door Is the Limit
344 hold requests were waiting on June 30, 2026
Mostly for the tile saw, the carpet cleaner and the pressure washer
Holds wait 11 days on average
On the 3 days we're open, a returned tool often goes back out within the hour
On the 4 days we're closed, it sits on the shelf

Slide 5: What We Do Now (FY2026)
1,962 active members, up from 1,410 a year earlier
9,840 tool loans, up from 7,215
2,350 tools on the shelves
14 repair cafes: 438 of 611 items fixed
46 volunteers gave 3,120 hours
Sliding-scale membership from $0 to $60; about 1 member in 4 pays nothing
58% would otherwise have bought the tool new
Members estimate they saved a median of $180 over the year

Slide 6: What Longer Hours Fix
Open 34 hours a week instead of 22
New: Tuesday and Thursday evenings until 8 p.m.
New: Saturday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
Shift workers and people with weekday jobs can finally reach us
Returned tools go back out sooner, so holds get shorter

Slide 7: Why It Takes a Paid Coordinator
A part-time coordinator, 25 hours a week
Volunteers can't cover every new shift
A trained lead must be on hand whenever power tools go out
The $46,500 covers the coordinator plus utilities and supplies for the longer hours

Slide 8: The Money
Ask: $46,500 a year for two years, $93,000 in all
FY2026 budget: $212,400, closed even, no debt
FY2027 budget for the board to take up: $258,900
Membership fees covered 29% of FY2026 costs
Each loan cost us about $21.60
Compare: a new tile saw costs about $400; a weekend store rental about $65

Slide 9: What We Expect, and How We'll Report
Our estimate: about 2,500 more loans a year once members learn the new times
That's a staff estimate, not a promise
At that level, each added loan would cost about $18.60
We will report the real results to the Fund
Contact: Rosa Delacroix-Imari, Director
